attachments.insertion_landmark: proximal phalanx of the little toe

actions: abducts and flexes the little toe

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Most lateral muscle of the first plantar layer, forming the lateral border of the foot -- the foot's structural mirror of abductor hallucis on the medial side.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

trigger_points.location_description: Muscle belly running along the lateral border of the sole, from the calcaneus to the base of the proximal phalanx of the little toe.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Pain that is largely confined to the muscle itself, over the lateral plantar edge of the foot beneath the fifth metatarsal head; occasionally pain extends proximally toward the ankle (mimicking a sprain) or distally to the base of the little toe.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Prolonged standing/walking, a laterally worn or ill-fitting shoe, and repetitive weight-bearing on the lateral foot border.
trigger_points.notes: Unlike many leg/foot trigger points, this one does not refer pain far from the muscle; the resulting limp or antalgic gait can be mistaken for an ankle sprain.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 2 (Lower Extremities), 1999 -- as cited in secondary summaries (e.g. Morningside Acupuncture NYC 'Abductor Digiti Minimi Trigger Points', triggerpoints.net) describing the lateral-foot/fifth-metatarsal-head referral pattern
